object_description: scaffold-like school volume organized around a flexible floor structure
design_condition: The large footprint retains a front zone toward the street and activates the park-facing head with an outdoor canteen area, while paths toward the park lack the desired spaciousness and scale.

positive.statement: The designers responded cleverly to flexible childcare-room use and organized the classroom floor plan logically without reducing its spatial qualities.

position.rationale: The broad frame-like volume anchors the unexposed classroom organization at mid-building level.

positive.statement: Unobstructed access and the function of the main access to the school were strengthened.

position.rationale: The front edge toward the street provides the constrained main-access location.

positive.statement: The park-side activation with an outdoor canteen area is welcomed in principle and was solved more consistently after revision.

position.rationale: The park-facing head is visibly distinct and provides the likely outdoor canteen zone.

positive.statement: The industrial-scaffolding analogy has proved its worth: the structure can respond to requirements and be converted into an atmospheric, flexible school space.

position.rationale: Repeated frame-like bands and modular massing visibly support the scaffolding analogy.

negative.statement: Because the footprint could not be reduced, some questions about the outdoor space remain only partially answered.

position.rationale: The large footprint leaves an adjacent open-space region whose qualities are being questioned.

negative.statement: Moving the required fenced kindergarten area into the park perimeter was critically questioned.

position.rationale: The park perimeter is approximated at the active head, without a distinguishable fence.

negative.statement: The proposed stone-slab paths lack the desired spaciousness and appropriate scale for future development.

position.rationale: Park-facing circulation is approximated along the open edge of the building footprint.

negative.statement: The ornamental wall for facade greening is difficult to evaluate in terms of greening success and maintenance.

position.rationale: The wall is not separable, so the marker uses a plausible side-envelope facade location.

negative.statement: The project suffers in particular from a lack of clarity in dealing with the required open spaces.

position.rationale: Open zones around the large footprint are visible, though their programmatic clarity is not.
